rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative exposes that lacking even one divine attribute precludes divinity; lacking all of them makes the idols' claim still more untenable.
rows.anchor: مع كل عاقل إذا تعقل أن لا تصح رتبة الإلهية مع فقد واحدة منها , فكيف مع فقدها كلها ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from a past time adverb to a present verb evokes the whole span of worship and rebukes them by asking whether the idols ever heard them.
rows.anchor: معبرا بظرف ماض وفعل مضارع تنبيها على استحضار جميع الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Benefit is the worshipper's primary aim; even something unable to hear might be worshipped for its own benefit or for harming an enemy, as fire can.
rows.anchor: وكان محط حال العابد والداعي بالقصد الول بالذات جلب النفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols have no power to hear, benefit, or harm, as their worshippers admit.
rows.anchor: لا والله ! ليس عندهم شيء من ذلك

rows.speaker: العبدة
rows.claim: The worshippers justify their practice by saying their earlier ancestors must have recognized something good in it and were wiser and more experienced.
rows.anchor: فلولا أنهم رأوا ذلك حسنان ما واظبوا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People would abandon a practice that caused visible physical harm, yet religious custom has long made false imitation easy to maintain.
rows.anchor: هذا الدين يهون على الناس فيه التقليد بالباطل قديما وحديثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham pushes their imitation to its limit: precedence is no proof, and age cannot turn falsehood into truth.
rows.anchor: فإن التقدم والأولوية لا تكون برهانا على الصحة , والباطل لا ينقلب حقا بالقدمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensive singular عدُوّ suffices for friend or enemy without a plural, and Abraham treats the idols as enemies by opposing and destroying them.
rows.anchor: أغنت في العدو والصديق عن صيغة الجمع ولا سيما وهي شبيهة بالمصادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham calls the idols his enemies and links this stance to his condemnation of ancestral idolatry, contempt for idols, and plan to destroy them.
rows.anchor: لقد كنتم أنتم وآباؤكم في ضلال مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord of all worlds is the exception because He governs the cosmos and is Abraham's ally and object of worship, not his enemy.
rows.anchor: أي مدبر هذه الأكوان كلها - كما قال موسى عليه السلام - لأن ذلك أشهر الأوصاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God alone created Abraham, only He can know a creature's inward state and control it completely; He has every perfection and can benefit or harm.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا يعلم باطن المخلوق ويقدر على كمال التصرف فيه غير خالقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human being has a bodily form from the realm of creation and a spiritual form from the realm of command; bodily formation comes first.
rows.anchor: والإنسان له قالب من عالم الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation is expressed in the past because it does not recur in this world, while guidance is present-tense because it recurs in religious and worldly life.
rows.anchor: وذكر الخلق بالماضي لأنه لا يتجدد في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone provides food and drink; He could remove what Abraham eats and drinks or afflict him so he cannot consume either.
rows.anchor: ولو أراد لأعدم ما آكل وما أشرب أو أصابني بآفة لا أستطيع معها أكلا ولا شربا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham courteously attributes illness to himself although all things are known to be from God; he describes illness as natural humours overcoming one another.
rows.anchor: نزهه عن نسبته إليه أدبا وإن كانت نسبة الكل إليه سبحانه معلومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone heals by balancing the humours and forcing them into harmony; doctors are secondary, and a person may bring illness on himself through cold, heat, food, or similar causes.
rows.anchor: تعديل المزاج بتعديل الأخلاط وقسرها على الاجتماع والاعتدالن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God causes bodily death despite efforts to avert it and spiritual death through ignorance despite efforts to resist it; He revives physically with spirit and spiritually through guidance for the afterlife's recompense.
rows.anchor: أي حسا وإن اجتهدت في دفع الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word ثم marks the greatness of resurrection and the long interval spent in the barzakh.
rows.anchor: أتى بأداة التراخي لذلك ولطول المكث في البرزخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham does not state exclusivity for giving life and death because only God had reported Nimrod's claim in al-Baqara; Abraham visibly demonstrated his inability to create a form, much less give or remove its spirit.
rows.anchor: ولم يأت هنا بما يدل على الحصر لأنه لا مدعي للإحياء والإماتة إلا ما ذكره سبحانه عن نمروج في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines hope as the mind's attachment to something without a prior cause; Abraham therefore does not claim that his deeds entitle him to forgiveness.
rows.anchor: كما قال الحرالي في البقرة تعلق البال بالشيء من غير تقدم سبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's language of hope humbles him and sets aside his works because he cannot give God His due; he calls the shortcoming his own out of humility.
rows.anchor: فلذلك لم يعد له عملا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness benefits the servant alone, since God is free of any self-serving purpose; it means erasing and covering the fault.
rows.anchor: فكانت المغفرة لحظ العبد ليس غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the shortcoming his own is humility before God: a weak servant cannot perform all that service to the mighty Lord requires, and every act depends on God's enabling.
rows.anchor: فإم الضعيف العاجز لا يبلغ كل ما ينبغي من خدمة العلي الكبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham praises God before asking, showing that beginning a supplication with praise is important and has a great effect on its acceptance.
rows.anchor: فدل صنيعه على أن تقديم الثناء على السؤال أمر مهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He asks for sound judgment: action made precise through knowledge and built according to what wisdom requires.
rows.anchor: وأصله بناء الشيء على ما توجبه الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joining the righteous is a request for pure grace, since scrutiny in accounting brings punishment; the righteous are leaders of the God-conscious in both worlds, with uncorrupted speech and action.
rows.anchor: وهم من كتن قوله وفعله صافيا عن شوب فساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A truthful tongue among later people means beautiful remembrance, broad acceptance, and praise for the good God made Abraham display, so he becomes an example for the pious.
rows.anchor: لسان صدق } أي ذكرا جميلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author invokes the saying that one who establishes a good practice earns its reward and the reward of everyone who follows it through the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: فإن ( من سن سنة حسنة كان له أجرها وأجر من عمل بها إلى يوم القيامة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answered by making Abraham a blessed source of prophets who renewed his remembrance, most notably through the Prophet's prayer formula for Muhammad as for Abraham.
rows.anchor: من قوله : ( صل على محمد كما صليت على إبراهيم ) إلى آخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Garden is reached only by God's favor, not by what a person has earned; inheritance aptly suggests receiving ownership without the heir's own acquisition.
rows.anchor: وكانت الجنة لا تنال إلا بمنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After praying for himself, Abraham prays for his father as the person most deserving of his kindness next.
rows.anchor: ولما دعا لنفسه , ثنى بأحق الخلق ببره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Abraham apparently made this prayer before learning that his father's misery was fixed.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا كان قل معرفته بتأييد شقائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plea not to be disgraced on resurrection day is made in the presence of people denying resurrection and challenges their idol worship.
rows.anchor: وكأن هذا الدعاء كان بحضورهم في الإنكار عليهم في عبادة الأصنام

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Biqai calls it authentic: Bukhari reports that Abraham asks what disgrace could exceed his father's fate; his father is changed into a ذيخ and cast into Hell, and God says Paradise is forbidden to unbelievers.
rows.anchor: كما رواه البخاري في غير موضع عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه , وأن الله تعالى يقول له : ( إني حرمت الجنة عل الكافرين )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author infers that Abraham's mother had believed: if she too were an unbeliever, Abraham would have asked forgiveness for her as well.
rows.anchor: ولو كانت أمه كافرة لسأله فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day wealth cannot ransom someone or be given to an intercessor or powerful defender, and sons cannot support or console; other things are even less useful.
rows.anchor: يفتدي به أو يبذله لشافع أو ناصر مقاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound heart is free of illness that alters its original God-given nature: Islam, headed by monotheism, upright good action, and adherence to the Sunna.
rows.anchor: عن افطرة الأولى التي فطره الله عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is grammatically an unexpressed exception after the negation; wealth and children benefit the sound-hearted through good use of them.
rows.anchor: والاستثناء مفرغ , والظاهر أن قوله { وأزلقت } أي قربت بأيسر وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Garden is brought near to the mindful, and the assembled people learn that it belongs specifically to them, hastening their joy and honor.
rows.anchor: وعرف أهل الموقف أنها لهم خاصة تعجيلا لسرورهم وزيادة في شرفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is a fiercely blazing fire, originally a great fire in a deep hollow, exposed to the astray so they know it is theirs.
rows.anchor: اي النار الشديدة التأجج , واصلها نار عظيمة في مهواة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker of the rebuke is left unnamed so it applies to anyone and to degrade the idolaters; the saying itself, not its speaker, is what wounds them.
rows.anchor: وأبهم القائل ليصلح لكل أحد , تحقيرا لهم , ولأن المنكى نفس القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot protect their worshippers from the exposed punishment or even defend themselves, despite the worshippers' claim that they would intercede and protect them.
rows.anchor: وكنتم تزعمون أنهم يشفعون لكم ويقونكم شر هذا اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols are hurled into Hell, overturned and thrown repeatedly and violently by those commanded to do so, visibly demonstrating their inability even before they answer.
rows.anchor: قلبوا وصرعوا ورموا , قلبا عظيما مكررا سريعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The group includes idols and similar objects, those misguided through them, and all of Iblis's forces, devils from both humans and jinn.
rows.anchor: أي الأصنام وما شابهها مما عبد من الشاطين ونحوهم

rows.speaker: العبدة
rows.claim: The worshippers argue with their idols in Hell and admit clear error: they equated them in rank with the Lord who created and governed them.
rows.anchor: إن كنا لفي ضلال مبين * } أي ظاهر جدا لمن كان له قلب { إذ } أي حين { نسويكم } في الرتبة

rows.speaker: العبدة
rows.claim: They blame only the criminals for leading them from the clear path; these are people deeply rooted in sin, severing every proper connection.
rows.anchor: أي العريقون في صفة الإجرام , المقتضي لقطع كل ما ينبغي أن يوصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They have no intercessors to get them into Paradise because they redirected what was due to God to beings with no authority.
rows.anchor: لأنا صرفنا ما كان يجب علينا لذي الأمر إلى من لا أمر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural intercessors may reflect that they had entered the matter of the great intercession.
rows.anchor: ولعله لم يفرد الشافع لأنهم دخلوا في الشفاعة العظمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great Throne contains all created worlds, while its Lord is greater than it and every great thing, as shown by the Throne Verse and other evidence.
rows.anchor: ثبت أن صاحبه أعظم منه ومن كل عظيم بآية الكرسي وبغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is a prostration verse under both readings: the doubled reading praises prostration and censures its omission, while the light reading commands prostration; both concern divine greatness.
rows.anchor: وهذه آية سجدة على كل القراءتين , لأن مواضع السجود إما مدح لمن أتى بها , أو ذم لمن تركها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon says he will test the report and determine whether the hoopoe spoke truth, which would excuse it, or lied.
rows.anchor: سننظر } أي نختبر ما قلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying the hoopoe was among the liars implies an ingrained liar, unlike saying it lied once, since lying to a prophet-king would show deep-rooted boldness.
rows.anchor: فإنه لا يجترىء على الكذب عندي إلا من كان عريقا في الكذب دون ( أم كذبت ) لأن هذا يصدق بمرة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon immediately writes a very brief letter to remove the wrong of sun-worship quickly if the hoopoe's report is true, and gives it to the ready bird.
rows.anchor: فكتب له كتابا على الفورفي غاية الوجازة قصدا للإسراع في إزالة المنكر على تقدير صدق الهدهد بحسب الاستطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The فاء signals urgency: the bird flies as swiftly as lightning with God's added help, honoring His prophet.
rows.anchor: أمده الله زيادة على ذلك بمعونة منه إكراما لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم فصار كأنه البرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon addresses the letter to the whole group because they worship the sun, emphasizing the importance of religion.
rows.anchor: أي الذين ذكرت أنهم يعبدون الشمس , وذلك للاهتمام بأمر الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After delivery, the hoopoe waits fluttering above them until they recognize the bearer, then withdraws to a safe place where it can hear their talk without being reached.
rows.anchor: أمره بأن يمكث بعد إلقائه يرفرف على رؤوسهم حتى يتحققوا أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Then marks the delay between delivery and withdrawal to let the recipients verify what happened.
rows.anchor: فاشار سبحانه إلى ذلك بأداة التراخي بقوله , { ثم } أي بعد وصولك وإلقائك { تول }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Queen gathers her people, or perhaps only the notables, before speaking; the author also says she was literate and from the people of Tubbaʿ.
rows.anchor: وكانت كاتبة نم قوم تبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive phrase saying that a letter was cast to her presents its delivery as strange and unexpected.
rows.anchor: فبنت للمفعول قولها : { إني ألقي إلي } أي بإلقاء ملق على وجه غريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She calls the letter noble because of the distinction of sender and messenger, its opening with God's greatest name, its brevity, and its complete meaning.
rows.anchor: منجهة المرسل والرسول والافتتاح بالاسم الأعظم إلى ما له من وجازة اللفظ وبلوغ المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming Solomon before the basmala does not detract from beginning with praise of God.
rows.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أن الابتداء باسم صاحب الكتاب لا يقدح في الابتداء بالحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala praises the supreme God, whose majesty and generosity encompass all and whose mercy grants special favors to whom He wills.
rows.anchor: فحمد المستحق للحمد وهو الملك الأعلى المحيط عظمه بدائرتي الجلال والإكرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After identifying the sender, the basmala names God as the one worthy of worship and signals Solomon's prophethood; this order favors acceptance because most people recognize truth through people.
rows.anchor: لأن أكثر الخلق إنما يعرف الحق بالرجال , ولما في كتابه من الدلالة على نبوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not exalt yourselves over me means do not refuse or resist my command as rulers do; abandon pride because Solomon calls them to God, on whom all movement and stillness depend.
rows.anchor: لا تمتنعوا من الإجابة لي , والإذعان لأمري , كما يفعل الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to come submitting means to arrive obedient and humbled in recognition of the miracle shown in the letter.
rows.anchor: أي منقادين خاضعين بما رأيتم من معجزتي في أمر الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Queen calls her request for advice a fatwa by extension: a fatwa answers a particular case with a sound judgment, and the word derives from youthful age.
rows.anchor: جعلت المشورة فتوى توسعا , لأن الفتوى الجواب في الحادثة , والحكم بما هو صواب مستعار من الفتاء في السن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Her regular consultation of her council on matters large and small shows courtesy and intelligence; the respect she shows them helps earn their obedience in ease and hardship.
rows.anchor: شأنها دائما مشاورتهم في كل جليل وحقير , فكيف بهذا الأمر الخطير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The council claims strength through wealth and men, and strong resolve in battle.
rows.anchor: نحن أولو قوة } أي بالمال والرجال { وأولو باس } أي عزم في الحرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The council leaves the choice of peace or confrontation to the Queen and says her orders will be obeyed.
rows.anchor: الأمر } راجع وموكول { إليك } اي كل من المسالمة والمصادمة { فانظري }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to persist in reciting and following the Qur'an as worship, convey the revelation without doubt, act on its commands, avoid its prohibitions, and let people rely on it because it gathers all knowledge.
rows.anchor: أواظب على تلاوته وتلوه - أي اتباعه - عبادة لربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever follows the Qur'an saves and benefits himself through reward and escape from punishment; whoever strays harms himself.
rows.anchor: لأنه يحييها بحوزة الثواب , ونجاته من العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's role toward one who strays is warning of the consequences of that person's deeds.
rows.anchor: أي المخوفين له عواقب صنعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise belongs to God in every outcome, whether everyone is guided, everyone strays, or people divide between the two, because nothing escapes His will.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا يخرج شيء عن مراده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises to show His signs in this life and the next, including events foretold or indicated in the Qur'an and His making Mecca briefly lawful for the Prophet; their fulfillment is certain.
rows.anchor: أي في الدنيا والآخرة بوعد محقق لا شك في وقوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the signs appear, people will recognize them from the Qur'an's descriptions, confirming its greatness and the truth of its message with certainty.
rows.anchor: لا تشكون في شيء من ذلك أنه على ما وصفته ولا ترتابون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the Lord is not heedless can grammatically be read as a circumstantial clause attached to the subject of يرى.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الجملة حالا من فاعل { يرى } أي ربكم غير غافل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the address reading, God is not unaware of the addressees' and their followers' obedience or sin, and will repay each according to what they deserve.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ بالخطاب كان المعنى : عما تعمل انت وأتباعك من الطاعة . وهو من المعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Delayed punishment does not mean God overlooks their deeds; He has set a term they will inevitably reach, and will raise the Prophet's standing while weakening his opponents according to His wisdom.
rows.anchor: فلا يظن ظان أن تركه للمعالجة بعقابهم لغفلة عن شيء من أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's ending returns to its opening by clarifying the Book, magnifying the Qur'an, and dividing people into guided and astray, joining the conclusion to the beginning through the Revealer's wisdom and knowledge.
rows.anchor: فقد رجع آخرها كما ترى بإبانة الكتاب وتفخيم القرآن وتقسيم الناس فيه إلى مهتد وضال
